cards.text: The prophet Jeremiah is still carrying the LORD's message about Babylon, and it is NOT good news for Babylon. Right in the middle of it, the LORD calls out to His own: 'My people!'

cards.question: The LORD calls out to His people living in Babylon. What does He tell them to do?
Why does the LORD tell His people to get out of Babylon?

answers.text: To save their lives from His anger
To bring Babylon's gold back home
To warn the cities around her

cards.text: Save your lives, each of you! If somebody had yelled that into my old junk drawer, I'd have been out before they hit the exclamation point, gold base and all.
Then He tells them about the news to come: a rumor one year, another the next, violence in the land and ruler against ruler. That's a group chat blowing up for YEARS, friend.

cards.question: When those rumors of violence and ruler against ruler come, the LORD tells His people to be afraid.

cards.text: The days are coming when the LORD will punish Babylon's idols, and her whole land will suffer shame. Then destroyers from the north will come against her.

cards.question: When the destroyers from the north come against Babylon, heaven and earth will mourn over her.

cards.text: Then the LORD says it straight: Babylon must fall. All over the earth, the slain have fallen because of her.

cards.question: The LORD is speaking to His own people. He says Babylon must fall on account of the slain of ___.

cards.text: Now He speaks up: 'You who have escaped the sword, depart and do not linger!' No snooze button on this one, friend. No 'five more minutes.'

cards.question: As the ones who escaped the sword head out, the LORD tells them what to keep in mind: 'Remember the LORD from far away, and let ___ come to mind.'

cards.text: Then voices answer back, and it's heavy: 'We are ashamed because we have heard reproach; disgrace has covered our faces.'

cards.question: Why do the people say disgrace has covered their faces?

answers.text: Foreigners entered the LORD's holy places
Their own king abandoned the city
Their harvest failed two years running

cards.text: So the LORD answers that shame. The days are coming when He will punish Babylon's idols, and the wounded will groan throughout her land.

cards.question: Even if Babylon climbs to the heavens and fortifies her lofty stronghold, the destroyers the LORD sends will still come against her.

cards.text: Building higher won't help her, friend. That's like moving your desk to the top floor to dodge a bill, and the bill just takes the elevator.
Then listen: a cry from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans, Babylon's people.

cards.question: The LORD is going to destroy Babylon. What does He say He'll do to her mighty voice?

cards.text: The waves will roar like great waters. A destroyer is coming against Babylon, and her warriors will be captured, their bows broken.

cards.question: A destroyer is coming against Babylon. What reason does the LORD give for it?

answers.text: The LORD will repay in full
Her bowmen ran out of arrows

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll make her princes and wise men drunk, along with her governors, officials and warriors. The whole leadership, friend. Top to bottom.

cards.question: After the LORD makes Babylon's leaders drunk, they will sleep it off and wake up the next morning.
Who puts His name on this word about Babylon's leaders?

answers.text: The King whose name is the LORD of Hosts

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts speaks about her defenses. Babylon's thick walls will be leveled.

cards.question: Babylon's thick walls get leveled. What happens to her high gates?
With Babylon's walls leveled and her gates burned, the LORD of Hosts says, 'So the labor of the people will be for ___.'

cards.text: The nations will exhaust themselves just to fuel the flames. That's like working overtime all month and watching the boss hit DELETE on your project.

findings.problem: This story card only re-tells Jeremiah 51:45, which cards 1 to 3 already covered, and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. It works as a recap card carrying a joke. The joke should ride along on a card that tells new passage content.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says he'd have left the junk drawer 'gold base and all.' In his backstory he didn't have the gold base in the drawer. He was standing on it only after the angel called him out and renewed him. The joke adds something new to his backstory.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The question says 'The LORD is speaking to His own people' for Jeremiah 51:49. The verse doesn't say who is being addressed, and it speaks of Israel in the third person.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote, 'No snooze button on this one, friend.' and 'No five more minutes.' That is more than the limit for a non-opening story card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card only re-tells Jeremiah 51:53, which card 2 already told and answered, and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The question asks why the destroyer is coming against Babylon. In Jeremiah 51:56, the clause 'for the LORD is a God of retribution; He will repay in full' follows the warriors being captured and their bows broken. The text doesn't directly tie it to the destroyer coming. The question makes a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the leaders made drunk, 'The whole leadership, friend.' and 'Top to bottom.' That is more than the limit for a non-opening story card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The King whose name is the LORD of Hosts,' is twice as long as the wrong answers and is the only one that sounds like the Bible. It stands out from 'Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon' and 'Cyrus king of Persia.'

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question asks 'Who puts His name on this word,' with a capital 'His.' The capital marks the speaker as God, which rules out both human kings before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: In 'the labor of the people will be for ___,' the wrong answer 'Israel' is a proper noun. The other two answers ('nothing' and 'glory') describe what the labor comes to. 'Israel' isn't the same kind of thing, and it doesn't make a believable reading of the line.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
